sections.html:
Marshalltown is the Marshall County seat in central Iowa, at about 899 feet of elevation, and covers roughly 19.2 square miles. Henry Anson, the first European settler, arrived in April 1851 and built a log cabin on high ground between the Iowa River and Linn Creek. The town was named Marshall in 1853 and became Marshalltown in 1862, and the county seat moved here from Marietta in 1863 after the railroad arrived.

The 2020 count was 27,591 residents, with a mid-2025 estimate of 27,536. The city has barely changed in size, since the counts were 26,009 in 2000 and 27,552 in 2010. A flat population means price and condition, not a rush of newcomers, decide most sales.

• Owner-occupied housing rate: 68.8 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $127,700.
  • Median gross rent: $891.
  • Households: 10,135, averaging 2.62 people.

These are 2020 to 2024 estimates.

Median value is modest, so even a mid-sized repair bill is a large share of what a house is worth. Many owners of older houses run that math before choosing between fixing the house and selling it as is. With households averaging 2.62 people, a three-bedroom family house is the kind of property many local buyers are shopping for.

Plant employment drives demand. JBS pork processing is the largest employer, followed by Emerson / Fisher Controls, and when a big employer changes shifts or headcount, buyers and renters shift with it.

An EF3 tornado crossed downtown Marshalltown on July 19, 2018, with peak winds of 145 mph. It stayed on the ground for 23 minutes along an 8.41 mile path up to 1,200 yards wide, destroyed the courthouse spire and injured 23 people, with no deaths. Two months later, city officials said more than 1,800 homes were affected and 60 carried condemnation placards. FEMA estimated that more than 2,000 buildings were damaged. An earlier F3 tornado hit the south side on April 23, 1961.

A derecho on August 10, 2020, with reported winds near 99 mph, brought a second round of damage and cost the city many park trees.

  • Find out whether past storm repairs were permitted and finished.
  • Keep roof and insurance records, since buyers and appraisers ask for them.
  • Expect inspectors to look hard at roofs, chimneys and trees near the house.
  • An unrepaired, storm-damaged house can still be sold as is for cash.

Every rental unit in Marshalltown has to be registered, and a new rental must pass inspection before a tenant moves in. Existing rentals pay $25 per unit for annual registration, with a $25 late fee per parcel plus finance charges. Rental units are generally inspected about every three years. A change of ownership for an already registered property is exempt from the application fee.

ChargeAmount
Application, new or newly rented empty unit$75
Application, previously occupied unit never registered$500
Inspection, first unit$90
Inspection, second unit$50

Inspection, complexes of 16 or more unitsCapped at $400

A buyer who plans to keep the house as a rental should ask whether the unit is registered and when it was last inspected. A $500 unregistered-unit fee is the kind of cost that can surprise a new owner. The Rental Housing Division answers at 641-754-6582.

The city's Code Enforcement Office handles nuisance abatement, property maintenance and zoning violations, with examples including tall grass, junk vehicles and garbage. Complaints can be made by phone, through the city's online form or in person at 36 N. Center Street.

An owner who receives a Code Violation Notice can use the city's appeal request form. Read any notice closely and call the office at 641-754-5759 to confirm the dates. Cash buyers can take a house with an open violation in its current state, which means the cleanup need not be done by closing.

Public schooling comes from the Marshalltown Community School District, with Marshalltown High School, six elementary schools, one intermediate school and a middle school for grades 7 and 8. The East Marshall district covers small parts of the city limits.

U.S. Route 30 bypasses the city to the south, Iowa Highway 14 runs through the center and Iowa Highway 330 is an expressway to Des Moines. Marshalltown Municipal Transit runs local buses, and the nearest commercial airport is Des Moines International, 53 miles southwest.

sections.h2: Marshall County taxes and the transfer tax
sections.html:
The county splits the tax bill into halves due September 1 and March 1, and each goes delinquent on October 1 or April 1. The Treasurer's office is in the courthouse at 1 E. Main Street, Suite 130, phone 641-754-6360.

Unpaid accounts receive notices on November 1 and May 1. A publication fee is added May 1, and from June 1 the delinquent parcels are advertised before the yearly tax sale. A parcel redeemed after the sale costs 2 percent interest per month, paid in guaranteed funds.

For the deed, Iowa Code 428A.1 sets the transfer tax at 80 cents per $500 of value above the first $500, and a declaration of value goes to the recorder with the deed.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Marshalltown house work?
sections.html:
With no mortgage to arrange, closing hinges on title work and your own calendar rather than a lender's.

  1. Send the address and the condition of the house.
  2. The buyer reviews it and makes an offer.
  3. If you want to proceed, a title company handles the deed and payoffs.
  4. Close and receive the proceeds.

This fits situations common in Marshalltown: a rental with deferred inspection items, a house with leftover storm damage, or an inherited property that nobody wants to renovate. You can say no and owe nothing.

sections.h2: Before you sell a rental or storm-damaged house
sections.html:
A few records make a Marshalltown sale simpler. For a rental, find the registration receipt and the date of the last inspection. For a storm-damaged house, pull together roof and insurance paperwork and any permit for work already done. For any house, ask the Marshall County Treasurer which halves are paid and whether a delinquency notice is outstanding.

Then decide what condition you are selling in. A cash buyer will take the house as is, but you get a better offer when you describe repairs, open notices and tenants honestly. Compare the number with your net from a listing after repairs, inspection credits and carrying costs.

Inherited houses often sit while the family decides what to do, and they pick up wear and notices in the meantime. Start by confirming whose names belong on the deed, because the title company needs the right signers. Next, check with the treasurer for unpaid halves and with Code Enforcement for open notices such as tall grass or junk vehicles.

If nobody wants to renovate, a cash buyer can take the house as it is. Tell the buyer about anything you know, from a leaking roof to a basement that stays wet, so the first offer reflects the house and does not change later.

faqs.q: How many homes did the 2018 Marshalltown tornado affect?
faqs.a: Two months after the tornado, city officials said more than 1,800 homes were affected and 60 had condemnation placards. FEMA estimated that more than 2,000 buildings were damaged.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Marshalltown?
faqs.a: Estimates for 2020 to 2024 put owner-occupied homes at $127,700 and gross rent at $891.

faqs.q: Do Marshalltown landlords have to register rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. New rental units must be registered and inspected before occupancy, and existing units pay $25 per unit each year. Rentals are generally inspected about every three years.

faqs.q: When are Marshall County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half is due September 1 and half on March 1. Delinquency starts October 1 for the first and April 1 for the second.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marshalltown house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers will take a house as is, even with open nuisance or maintenance notices. Read the notice and talk to the Code Enforcement Office about deadlines before you sign anything.
